intro: Imagine a workshop where the sculptors simply put down their tools and never came back. You are at Yesemek Quarry and Sculpture Workshop in Gaziantep province, worked from the 14th to the 8th century BC. It is the largest known open-air sculpture workshop of the Near East: more than three hundred half-finished lions, sphinxes and mountain gods lie across the slope, exactly where they were left.
history: The workshop opened in the fourteenth century BC under the Hittite empire, and carried on into the eighth under the Neo-Hittite states. On the slope where the basalt was quarried, more than three hundred roughed-out sculptures still lie where they were left: gate lions, sphinxes and mountain gods. Why so many unfinished? Because the workshop was abandoned suddenly under Assyrian attack, and the whole production process froze in place.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the gate lions and the sphinxes, look for the mountain god figures, and take in the quarry slope itself.
facts: Did you know? Every sculpture here is unfinished. More than three hundred half-finished lions, sphinxes and mountain gods lie on the slope where they were left. The workshop was abandoned suddenly under Assyrian attack, so the process simply froze. That is the gift of Yesemek: every stage, from rough blocking to final carving, can be seen side by side on this one slope.
outro: This brings our journey through Yesemek Quarry and Sculpture Workshop to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These figures have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
